title: Scalar restriction normalizes the singleton direct-image evaluation comparison
statement:
Let $u:\mathscr X\to\mathscr Y$ be a geometric morphism of topoi presented by sites small in the module universe, let $A_Y$ be a sheaf of commutative rings and put $A_X=u^{-1}A_Y$ [def-weil-size-convention], [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Let $B_Y$ be an inverse sequence of commutative ring sheaves, with a compatible map $\Delta A_Y\to B_Y$, and put $B_X=u^{-1}B_Y$ with its pulled-back algebra structure. Strict $B_T$-systems and constant-$A_T$ towers are modules on the vertical diagram sites [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site], [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Work in ordinary unbounded derived module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $U_T$ forget $B_T$ to constant-$A_T$ towers, let $r_{T,n}$ forget $B_{T,n}$ to $A_T$, and let $e_n^T,e_n^A$ be exact evaluations. Write $P_B=Ru_{*,B_\bullet}$, $P_A^J=Ru_{*,A}^{J}$, $P_A=Ru_{*,A}$ and $P_n=Ru_{*,B_n}$ for the canonical derived direct images, with module-induced adjunctions. Let $G_B,u_n^*$ be the corresponding exact inverse images.

Let $L_n^T\dashv e_n^T$ be the singleton derived adjunctions. Define $\beta^B_{n,Z}:e_n^YP_BZ\xrightarrow{\sim}P_ne_n^XZ$ by the natural Hom bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(V,e_n^YP_BZ)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G_BL_n^YV,Z)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_n^Xu_n^*V,Z)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(V,P_ne_n^XZ),$$
where the middle bijection uses $c_n^{-1}$ from [lem-pur-system-singleton-geometric-pullback]. Use the singleton/scalar isomorphisms $S_\bullet L_n\cong L_nS_n$ of [lem-pur-system-singleton-scalar-extension], normalized as conjugates of commuting exact scalar restriction and evaluation, for the maps $\Delta A_T\to B_T$. Let $\delta:U_YP_B\xrightarrow{\sim}P_A^JU_X$ be the two-factorization comparison of [lem-pur-diagram-ring-restriction-pushforward], let $\kappa_n:r_{Y,n}P_n\xrightarrow{\sim}P_Ar_{X,n}$ be the coefficient-restriction/direct-image comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], and let $\beta^A_n:e_n^AP_A^J\xrightarrow{\sim}P_Ae_n^A$ be the constant-ring tower comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-tower-derived-evaluation-normalization]. Then, under the ordinary restriction/evaluation identifications,
$$\kappa_{n,e_n^XZ}\circ r_{Y,n}(\beta^B_{n,Z})=\beta^A_{n,U_XZ}\circ e_n^A(\delta_Z).$$
The singleton Hom construction also has counit identity
$$e_n^X(\varepsilon^B_Z)=\varepsilon^{(n)}_{e_n^XZ}\circ u_n^*(\beta^B_{n,Z}).$$
For $m\ge n$, $\beta^B_m,\beta^B_n$ intertwine the actual restriction-form transition of $P_BZ$ with $P_m$ of the transition of $Z$, followed by the canonical restriction/direct-image comparison from $B_m$ to $B_n$. These identities hold naturally for all derived $Z$, using the specified adjunctions, without preservation of K-injectives by varying-ring evaluation or flatness of any coefficient map.

proof.text: Construct the normalized level scalar and transition squares from inverse-image scalar restriction. Extend them to the whole system and use the invertible derived restriction mates and their scalar/transition coherence.
Identify the specified geometric singleton conjugate with the actual derived evaluation mate.

Define delta and kappa as the isomorphisms of their derived mates, and chi as the inverse. The general derived exact mate factorization proves all resolution-unit equations. Conjugate counit and naturality prove the Hom clause. Mate-counit transposition proves the evaluated counit, and substitution into the two coherence identities proves the remaining scalar and transition clauses.

The statement is pinned throughout (β^B_n by the singleton Hom chain; δ, κ_n, β^A_n by named nodes). It holds in the small cases u=id, B=ΔA, j>n, m=n and nonflat Z→Z/2. I recomputed every conjugation direction. Step 1: β^B_n is the conjugate of c_n^{-1}. Step 2: the counit identity follows from e_n c_n=1 and the triangle identity. Step 3: under lem-sfb-ringed-comparison-tensor-adjunction applied to the two paths, (λ^{-1})^c=δ and (λ_n^{-1})^c=κ_n; the square of ring maps commutes because B_X=u^{-1}B_Y. Step 4: β̃^A=β^A by uniqueness of the adjunct under the tower-normalization counit equation. Steps 6-7: the left square equals b⊗u^{-1}q on both paths at j≤n, and mate pasting gives κ r(β^B)=β^A e^A(δ). Steps 8-9: the conjugate of the transition is the lower-singleton map, by systemSingleDerivedTranspose (read in lean/Sheaf/CategoryTheory/SystemSingleDerivedEvaluation.lean). χ=(λ_{m,n})^c: P_m R_X→R_Y P_n, and conjugating gives R_Y(β_n)t^Y=χP_m(t^X)β_m. Fault fixed (C1/C4): Step 6 computes the pullback-composition comparisons λ, λ_n by their ordinary maps on flat-term K-flat complexes, but no step cited lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback, which states this (ε_P iso, compatible with composition). I added it to Step 5 (text, uses, proof_deps) and declared it as a tool use. Adding it creates no cycle. lean.note: The direct images are the canonical total right derived functors of ordinary module right adjoints, with the induced derived adjunctions. The beta comparisons are actual conjugateIsoEquiv constructions from the fully normalized geometric singleton comparison. The conclusion constructs the ordinary scalar/restriction squares with fixed underlying maps and supplies delta, kappa and chi with both mate and resolution-unit characterizations; it then states the scalar square, evaluated counit and actual strict transition identities. Constant-ring systems use their ringed-sequence-site presentation of ordinary towers. Site universes remain independent.
